3: # TiffCraft
4: 
5: TiffCraft is a header-only C++ library for working with TIFF images. At the
6: moment, it requires C++20 or newer and contains functionality for reading TIFF
7: images in various uncompressed formats.
8: 
9: # Objectives
10: 
11: TiffCraft is designed based on the following principles:
12: 
13: - Permissive license: to be used in open source and proprietary software.
14: - C++ header-only: to easy integration onto existing projects.
15: - Flexible but simple API: for ease of use.
16: - Feature complete: to cover a wide variety of use cases.
17:   - TiffCraft is NOT feature complete at this time! The objective is for guiding
18:     on-going development.
19: 
20: # Building from source
21: 
22: Prerequisites: CMake >= 3.22, a C++20 compiler, git, and git-lfs.
23: 
24: Clone the repository with its submodules:
25: 
26: ```sh
27: git clone --recursive https://github.com/danielm5/tiffcraft.git
28: ```
29: 
30: Existing clones can fetch the fixtures with:
31: 
32: ```sh
33: git submodule update --init --recursive
34: ```
35: 
36: The test fixtures live in the `tests/libtiff-pics` submodule and are stored
37: in Git LFS. On Debian, install git-lfs with `sudo apt install git-lfs`.
38: `./build.sh` runs the submodule and LFS steps for you; otherwise pull the
39: fixtures manually:
40: 
41: ```sh
42: git -C tests/libtiff-pics lfs pull
43: ```
44: 
45: Build (`./build.sh` without arguments auto-picks a preset on Linux, Windows,
46: and macOS):
47: 
48: ```sh
49: ./build.sh
50: ```
51: 
52: Or pass an explicit preset (e.g. `gcc-linux-release`, listed in
53: `CMakePresets.json`):
54: 
55: ```sh
56: ./build.sh gcc-linux-release
57: ```
58: 
59: Run the tests:
60: 
61: ```sh
62: ctest --preset gcc-linux-release --output-on-failure
63: ```
64: 
65: or `./run_test.sh`.
66: 
67: Note: without git-lfs the checkout keeps Git LFS pointer files instead of
68: real TIFFs, and the tests will fail with "Invalid byte order in TIFF header".
69: To remedy, run:
70: 
71: ```sh
72: git submodule update --init --recursive && git -C tests/libtiff-pics lfs pull
73: ```
74: 
75: # Usage
76: 
77: For quick access to TIFF image pixel data with individual pixels aligned to
78: word boundaries (i.e. 8 bits, 16 bits, or 32 bits), you could use code like
79: the following:
80: 
81: ```C++
82: #include <tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp>
83: #include <functional>
84: 
85: int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
86:   if (argc < 2) { return 1; }
87:   TiffCraft::TiffExporterAny tiffExporter;
88:   TiffCraft::load(argv[1], std::ref(tiffExporter), loadParams);
89:   auto image = iffExporter.takeImage();
90: 
91:   // your own image processing code
92: 
93:   return 0;
94: }
95: ```
96: 
97: TiffExporterAny will decode and convert pixels to a flat-buffer (i.e.
98:  `std::vector<std::byte>`) with 1, 2, or 4 bytes per sample the source pixel
99: format. For example, an image with 2-bits per sample is exported as an 8-bit
100: image.
101: 
102: # Advanced usage
103: 
104: Users that prefer to decode and handle the image pixel data themselves, or need
105: to handle multiple frames per image, could write their own handler:
106: 
107: ```C++
108: #include <tiffcraft/TiffImage.hpp>
109: #include <iostream>
110: 
111: int main() {
112:   TiffCraft::load("image.tiff",
113:     [](const TiffCraft::TiffImage::Header& header,
114:         const TiffCraft::TiffImage::IFD& ifd,
115:         TiffCraft::TiffImage::ImageData imageData) {
116:       std::cout << "Loaded IFD with " << ifd.entries().size()
117:                 << " entries." << std::endl;
118:       std::cout << "Image data size: " << imageData.size() << std::endl;
119: 
120:       // Add your own image processing code here
121: 
122:     });
123: 
124:   return 0;
125: }
126: ```
127: 
128: # Features
129: 
130: TiffCraft supports the following features:
131: 
132: - Reading TIFF images
133:   - Read and display image metadata
134:   - Bilevel, grayscale, palette-color, and RGB images
135:     - Varying number of bits per sample
136:     - RGB images are supported only for 3-channel images (no extra samples)
137: - Compression is NOT supported yet.
138: - Writing TIFF images is NOT supported yet.
139: 
140: Advanced users could use TiffCraft for other configurations than those
141: enumerated above by writing their customizing any of the existing exporter
142: classes, or writing their own from scratch.

3: # TiffCraft
4: 
5: TiffCraft is a header-only C++ library for working with TIFF images. At the
6: moment, it requires C++20 or newer and contains functionality for reading TIFF
7: images in various uncompressed formats.
8: 
9: # Objectives
10: 
11: TiffCraft is designed based on the following principles:
12: 
13: - Permissive license: to be used in open source and proprietary software.
14: - C++ header-only: to easy integration onto existing projects.
15: - Flexible but simple API: for ease of use.
16: - Feature complete: to cover a wide variety of use cases.
17:   - TiffCraft is NOT feature complete at this time! The objective is for guiding
18:     on-going development.
19: 
20: # Building from source
21: 
22: Prerequisites: CMake >= 3.22, a C++20 compiler, git, and git-lfs.
23: 
24: Clone the repository with its submodules:
25: 
26: ```sh
27: git clone --recursive https://github.com/danielm5/tiffcraft.git
28: ```
29: 
30: Existing clones can fetch the fixtures with:
31: 
32: ```sh
33: git submodule update --init --recursive
34: ```
35: 
36: The test fixtures live in the `tests/libtiff-pics` submodule and are stored
37: in Git LFS. On Debian, install git-lfs with `sudo apt install git-lfs`.
38: `./build.sh` runs the submodule and LFS steps for you; otherwise pull the
39: fixtures manually:
40: 
41: ```sh
42: git -C tests/libtiff-pics lfs pull
43: ```
44: 
45: Build (`./build.sh` without arguments auto-picks a preset on Linux, Windows,
46: and macOS):
47: 
48: ```sh
49: ./build.sh
50: ```
51: 
52: Or pass an explicit preset (e.g. `gcc-linux-release`, listed in
53: `CMakePresets.json`):

55: ```sh
56: ./build.sh gcc-linux-release
57: ```
58: 
59: Run the tests:
60: 
61: ```sh
62: ctest --preset gcc-linux-release --output-on-failure
63: ```
64: 
65: or `./run_test.sh`.
66: 
67: Note: without git-lfs the checkout keeps Git LFS pointer files instead of
68: real TIFFs, and the tests will fail with "Invalid byte order in TIFF header".
69: To remedy, run:
70: 
71: ```sh
72: git submodule update --init --recursive && git -C tests/libtiff-pics lfs pull
73: ```
74: 
75: # Usage
76: 
77: For quick access to TIFF image pixel data with individual pixels aligned to
78: word boundaries (i.e. 8 bits, 16 bits, or 32 bits), you could use code like
79: the following:
80: 
81: ```C++
82: #include <tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp>
83: #include <functional>
84: 
85: int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
86:   if (argc < 2) { return 1; }
87:   TiffCraft::TiffExporterAny tiffExporter;
88:   TiffCraft::load(argv[1], std::ref(tiffExporter), loadParams);
89:   auto image = iffExporter.takeImage();
90: 
91:   // your own image processing code
92: 
93:   return 0;
94: }
95: ```
96: 
97: TiffExporterAny will decode and convert pixels to a flat-buffer (i.e.
98:  `std::vector<std::byte>`) with 1, 2, or 4 bytes per sample the source pixel
99: format. For example, an image with 2-bits per sample is exported as an 8-bit
100: image.
101: 
102: # Advanced usage
103: 
104: Users that prefer to decode and handle the image pixel data themselves, or need
105: to handle multiple frames per image, could write their own handler:
106: 
107: ```C++
108: #include <tiffcraft/TiffImage.hpp>
109: #include <iostream>
110: 
111: int main() {
112:   TiffCraft::load("image.tiff",
113:     [](const TiffCraft::TiffImage::Header& header,
114:         const TiffCraft::TiffImage::IFD& ifd,
115:         TiffCraft::TiffImage::ImageData imageData) {
116:       std::cout << "Loaded IFD with " << ifd.entries().size()
117:                 << " entries." << std::endl;
118:       std::cout << "Image data size: " << imageData.size() << std::endl;
119: 
120:       // Add your own image processing code here
121: 
122:     });
123: 
124:   return 0;
125: }
126: ```
127: 
128: # Features
129: 
130: TiffCraft supports the following features:
131: 
132: - Reading TIFF images
133:   - Read and display image metadata
134:   - Bilevel, grayscale, palette-color, and RGB images
135:     - Varying number of bits per sample
136:     - RGB images are supported only for 3-channel images (no extra samples)
137: - Compression is NOT supported yet.
138: - Writing TIFF images is NOT supported yet.
139: 
140: Advanced users could use TiffCraft for other configurations than those
141: enumerated above by writing their customizing any of the existing exporter
142: classes, or writing their own from scratch.

the 131-byte pointer files while the worktree holds real content, so without
it the submodule stays permanently dirty.

# Building from source

in Git LFS. On Debian, install git-lfs with `sudo apt install git-lfs`.

lfs pull`): the parent repository has no LFS objects, so a root-level

```sh
git clone --recursive https://github.com/danielm5/tiffcraft.git
```

Existing clones can fetch the fixtures with:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
git -C tests/libtiff-pics lfs pull
```

./build.sh

./build.sh gcc-linux-release

the 131-byte pointer files while the worktree holds real content, so without
